title: Answering the Parent's Open Question
content: The parent triangle-inequality-oq-06 records the three-point reverse triangle inequality |d(x,z) − d(y,z)| ≤ d(x,y) and explicitly poses, in its open-questions list, the n-point telescoping refinement. This file answers it: when the two endpoints are joined by a whole polygonal chain x₀, x₁, …, xₙ, the distance from a moving point to a fixed reference w changes by at most the total path length, |d(x₀,w) − d(xₙ,w)| ≤ Σ d(xᵢ,xᵢ₊₁). This is the reverse companion of the classical polygon inequality d(x₀,xₙ) ≤ Σ d(xᵢ,xᵢ₊₁). The core inequality is short; the substance is the sharpness layer certifying the bound is attained. Everything is 0-axiom (only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
mathContext: $|d(x_0,w)-d(x_n,w)| \le \sum_{i<n} d(x_i,x_{i+1})$ — the reverse companion of the polygon inequality.

title: The Telescoping Reverse Inequality
content: telescoping_reverse_triangle is the main result: |d(f₀,w) − d(fₙ,w)| ≤ Σ_{i<n} d(fᵢ,fᵢ₊₁). Its proof is a two-step composition — the three-point reverse inequality abs_dist_sub_le gives |d(f₀,w) − d(fₙ,w)| ≤ d(f₀,fₙ), and the polygon inequality dist_le_range_sum_dist gives d(f₀,fₙ) ≤ Σ d(fᵢ,fᵢ₊₁); .trans chains them. telescoping_reverse_triangle_one_sided strips the absolute value. reverse_triangle_of_telescoping specialises to n = 1 and recovers the parent's three-point reverse inequality |d(x,w) − d(y,w)| ≤ d(x,y), witnessing that the telescoping form genuinely generalises it.
mathContext: $n = 1$ recovers $|d(x,w)-d(y,w)| \le d(x,y)$; general $n$ bounds the change by the total path length.

title: The Faithful Problem Statement
content: telescoping_reverse_triangle_stated records the problem statement verbatim: with a side point y joined to x₀ by a single edge, |d(x₀,xₙ) − d(y,xₙ)| ≤ d(x₀,y) + Σ d(xᵢ,xᵢ₊₁). Because the three-point reverse inequality already gives |d(x₀,xₙ) − d(y,xₙ)| ≤ d(x₀,y) on its own, the nonnegative chain sum only slackens the bound; the proof is abs_dist_sub_le plus Finset.sum_nonneg and linarith. The genuinely tight statement is the plain telescoping form above.

title: Sharpness — the New Content
content: telescoping_reverse_triangle_sharp_mono is the original contribution: for a monotone real chain a₀ ≤ a₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ aₙ ≤ w, the telescoping bound is an EQUALITY. Both sides equal aₙ − a₀: the path sum telescopes (each edge dist(aᵢ,aᵢ₊₁) opens to aᵢ₊₁ − aᵢ by monotonicity, then Finset.sum_range_sub collapses the sum to aₙ − a₀), and on the left w lies beyond the whole chain so d(a₀,w) − d(aₙ,w) = (w − a₀) − (w − aₙ) = aₙ − a₀. Hence no coefficient in the bound can be lowered and no edge dropped. telescoping_reverse_triangle_sharp_witness pins the concrete 0,1,2 chain with w = 10: |10 − 8| = 1 + 1.

title: Axiom Audit
content: All six theorems depend only on the ordinary foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound — verified with #print axioms. There is no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool, and no decide / native_decide anywhere, so the entry is genuinely 0-axiom / 0-sorry and carries the verified badge.
